rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

recQOLj1bGHrs7YCW.Bio: Michelle Lundquist describes herself as a folk herbalist, gardener and homemaker with a passion for plants and their ability to heal. She has studied and actively worked with herbs since 2013, drawing most of her knowledge from hands on experience and mentors of the wise woman tradition, and a do it yourself spirit runs through her work as she encourages people to take their wellbeing into their own hands. She hosted more than eighty episodes of The Healing Home podcast as a kitchen witch, homemaker and folk herbalist, and now co-hosts Symbolic Studies with her husband Mario Garza.
recQOLj1bGHrs7YCW.Name: Michelle Lundquist

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Chance's Path Into Biofield Tuning", "body": "Chance said he began in 2019 after hearing Eileen Day McKusick, founder of Biofield Tuning, speak, and he recommended her books Tuning the Human Biofield and Electric Body, Electric Health. He described first buying a sonic slider, a weighted tuning fork, and said using it on a stubborn shoulder injury restored his range of motion within days. Chance said he spent 2020 and 2021 practicing on people before taking clients in earnest. He compared tuning to an oil change for the biofield and said he hopes people tuning each other becomes as common as doing laundry."}, {"title": "Forks, Intention, and the Candle Table", "body": "Chance described the tuning forks as a detection tool rather than the healing itself, and said attention and intention matter more than how well a client hears the sound. He explained that he lays out candles and crystals as a stand-in body on a table, points until he gets a hit, then chooses a fork the same way. He said a hit shows up as his ears popping, and that he sometimes receives images about a client's past, which he voices aloud. Chance then led a group tuning of nearly half an hour, working on the toroidal field, hips, shoulders, and sacral chakra."}, {"title": "Obstacles, Energy, and Staying Present", "body": "Chance said that keeping your own energy in your own battery, a line he credited to Owen Benjamin, helps a person remember what they already know. He argued that nobody can pull another person out of a funk, and described obstacles as the course rather than roadblocks. Michelle shared that being present is more than half the battle, and both agreed a partner who gives honest feedback is a gift. Chance added that balance is ongoing maintenance, like washing windows, rather than a state of being finished with healing."}, {"title": "Lymph, Herbs, and Frequency as Stillness", "body": "Michelle, an herbalist, named cleavers and calendula as plants she associated with moving lymph, and said she thought fear could block it. Chance described using a weighted tuning fork on the cheekbone as a gentler alternative to painful self-massage. Michelle also noticed the words frequency and frequently sound alike, which led Chance to describe raise your vibration as being centered. He said a very fast frequency would look like a still line, like a spinning top, and that the goal was finding stillness rather than literally vibrating more."}, {"title": "Coherence, EMF, and Sound Across Cultures", "body": "Michelle asked about sound used in harmful ways, and Chance said he believed a coherent energy field shields a person from EMF, citing metronomes that fall into sync as an example of nature ordering itself. He also described orgone devices made by a friend, and said he thought they changed conditions near cell towers. Chance recounted ancient Chinese dynasties retuning music and measurements to a new tonal center, and wondered whether that was tyranny or guardianship. Michelle shared that she had once called turkeys with her voice."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: The excellent Michelle Lundquist invited me to talk tuning on her new podcast, Michelle's Healing Home. Stick around to the end to receive a group tuning session!

How often are you getting yo-yo to the left or the right, the ups and the downs, the highs and the lows? I want people tuning each other to be as common knowledge as how to do your laundry.
